name: Boston
description: Boston is an 18th-century French trick-taking game that represents a pivotal transition from Whist to modern Bridge. Played by four individuals with a standard 52-card deck, it introduced a sophisticated bidding system where players compete for contracts ranging from winning a few tricks to 'Misère' (winning none) or 'Grand Slam' (winning all). It is famous for its complex scoring tables and the use of two decks to track game state, embodying the intellectual rigor of Enlightenment-era social card play.

history.origins: Despite its name, Boston likely originated in France during the American Revolutionary War (circa 1770s), named in honor of the siege of Boston. It was a favorite of French naval officers and rapidly spread to the United States and across Europe.
timeline: 1770s: Boston emerges in French salons as a 'revolutionary' Whist variant.
1800s: Becomes extremely popular in the United States and Russia (featured in Tolstoy's 'War and Peace').
1900s: Superseded by Auction Bridge but survives in traditional clubs.
Present: A rare specialty game played by card game historians and historical reenactors.
history.cultural: Portrayed in 19th-century literature as the game of the intellectual and social elite. Its complexity reflected the high-stakes diplomacy of the era.
history.evolution: Boston was the first major game to introduce a full hierarchy of contracts (bids), a concept that would later become the core of Bridge. It also introduced the idea of 'Misère' bids into the Whist family.

setup.deck: Standard 52-card French pack. Two packs are often used: one for play and one for determining trump rotation.
setup.dealing: Deal 13 cards to each player (usually in batches of 4-4-5).
setup.equipment: Standard pack, extensive scoring counters (fiches), and a specific Boston score table.

rules.objective: Win tricks according to the level of the declared contract. Higher contracts pay more but carry greater penalties.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Auction**: Players bid for contracts (e.g., 'Boston' for 8 tricks, 'Petit Misère' for zero). 2. **Trump**: The suit of the turned-up card from the second deck usually determines the 'preference' suit for trumps. 3. **The Play**: Standard trick-taking rules. Must follow suit. 4. **Tricks**: Highest trump wins; else highest card of led suit wins.
keyRules: Preference Suit: One suit (usually Diamonds) is the 'Preference' and outranks other suits in the auction.
Misère: A contract to lose every trick; there are no trumps in Misère hands.
Independence: Unlike Whist, you usually play alone against the other three defenders.

strategy.basic: Evaluate your hand for both high-trick potential and low-trick potential. A hand with many 7s and 8s is perfect for a Misère bid.
strategy.intermediate: Auction Tactics: Use the 'Preference' suit to overcall opponents even if your trick count is lower. Knowing when to 'Double' an opponent's contract is key to defensive scoring.
strategy.advanced: Defensive Coordination: Since three players defend against one declarer, they must cooperate to force the declarer to win (in Misère) or lose (in Boston) tricks. Lead through the declarer to trap their high cards.
tips: Don't bid Boston (8 tricks) without at least four solid trumps and an Ace in a side suit.
Watch the 'Independence' bids carefully—they are the highest-scoring and highest-risk plays.

variations.name: Boston de Fontainebleau
variations.description: A more elaborate 19th-century French version with even more contract levels and complex scoring.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variation rules are documented in text, but specific engine overrides for additional contracts and scoring tables are not yet encoded.

variations.name: Russian Boston
variations.description: Favored by the Russian nobility; uses a simplified auction but higher stakes for Misère.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Russian Boston adjusts auction structure and stakes, but dedicated engine override paths for its scoring and bidding have not yet been modeled.

scoring.description: Scoring is performed via a detailed table matching bid level to result. Losers pay declarer, or declarer pays each defender.
scoring.winCondition: Highest point total after a set number of hands.

synthesis.shortDescription: The missing link between Whist and Bridge. Boston is a masterful game of individual skill where you bid for contracts against three defending rivals. Whether chasing a Grand Slam or hiding in a Misère, the psychological battle of the auction is where the true game is won.

hero.title: BOSTON
hero.subtitle: The Enlightenment Duel
hero.tagline: Bid the siege. Hold the line. Outwit the three.
